On Sept 16th, in Voi, 2 herders were killed and other 3 injured in suspected retiliatory attacks The two herdsmen were suspected to have killed a boda boda driver, who was later found dumped in a forest.
On 15 September 2019, during an Isiolo-Garissa border attack, three herdsmen were killed and 100 camels stolen by unidentified individuals in Garba Tula.

On or before Sept 10th, camel herders attacked 3 men in Mutha. 1 Man was killed and other 2 suffered injuries. This action allegedly occurred as a consequence of the attack of Sept 7th in Ingo village (Isiolo).

On 8 September 2019, pastoralists attacked civilians at unspecified locations in Kitui East and West constituencies (Kitui county), killing 2. Two events coded at Malalani and Kakeani (at geoprec2), with 1 fatality each.

On 8 September 2019, pastoralists attacked civilians at unspecified locations in Kitui East and West constituencies (Kitui county), killing 2. Two events coded at Malalani and Kakeani (at geoprec2), with 1 fatality each.
25 Aug. Five people were killed in an attack carried out by suspected militias from Ethiopia in Forole, Marsabit County, Kenya. They also took unknown number of their cows.

25 Aug. Unidentified armed men from Ethiopia attacked the herders in Sabareh, Marsabit County, Kenya. Five herders killed in the attack. The suspected militias took unknown number of their cows and crossed the border into Ethiopia.
On Aug 25th 2019, in Safarisi, herders and farmers clashed over pasture. Farmers accused the herders (mostly from Tana River and Garissa counties) of grazing animals on their farms. A man was killed.

Around Jul 4th 2019 (exact date not reported) a herder in Sangailu was burnt with a hot object by a soldier. A video, which got frequent airplay on the internet, shows a senior military officer calming down residents, promising to take the victim for treatment.
02 July: Unidentified armed group killed one person and stole 150 cows in Sololo, Marsabit County.

Around 30 June 2019 (as reported), Pokot, elders and youths from Pokot and Turkana communities met in Kitale (Sabaoti, Trans Nzoia) and signed a peace agreement to end cattle rustling and border conflict.
On Jun 14th 2019, in Quri area of Garba Tula, Borana and Somalis clashed. Five people, among which a young girl, were killed. Several were injured.
On 22 May 2019, 2 herders were attacked in Fora by unidentified armed individuals who ambushed their house. The motives behind the attack are unclear.

On 19 May 2019, over 100 suspected Pokot militia armed with AK47 rifles attacked the Arabal area (Marigat, Baringo]. Two people sustained gunshot wounds during the incident and over 300 cattle were stolen.
On 18 May 2019, a man (presumbably a herder) was shot and injured by unknown gunmen in Fora. No fatalities reported.

In May 2019 (exact date not reported), Borana and Somalis clashed in El Digale, at the Isiolo-Garissa border (location coded as Garba Tula with GP2, for unfound El Digale). Two teenage herders were killed and one injured.
On 5 May 2019, around 50 suspected Samburu militia attacked Somali herders near Gotu grazing area (Merti, Isiolo), and made away with hundreds of goats and sheep.

notes: On 5 May 2019, national police reservists clashed with suspected Samburu militia [coded as Gotu, Merti, Isiolo], while pursuing stolen livestock [coded separately]. Four NPRs were killed during the incident.

On Mar 24th 2019, at the border of Isiolo and Garissa counties (coded as Mado Gashi with GP2) two herders were killed. The motives of the clash, according to authorities, might be linked to natural resoucers, as the two herders were killed at water points.
On 3 March 2019, clashes between Somali and Borana livestock traders erupted in Meru (Municipality, Imenti North, Meru). 4 people were killed, several were injured and one is missing.
27 February: A civilian was shot and killed by 'bandits' while herding his livestock in Kambi in West Pokot, on the Kainuk-Kapenguria road (approx coordinates used). No looting reported.
27 February: A civilian shot dead by armed men in Kainuk in retliation for an earlier attack on a herder in Kambi.

notes: On 21 February 2019, suspected Pokot militia shot dead five police reservists at Kapindasum (Marigat, Baringo), before making away with unknown number of livestock.

notes: On 16 February 2019, suspected Pokot clashed with Police reservists at Kainuk (Turkana South, Turkana). Two police reservists were killed, and a herder injured during the incident.

On 15 February 2019, a group of cattle rustlers ambushed a herders group near Ngomorosio seasonal river in Marti (Nachola, Samburu North, Samburu). There was an exchange of fire and several herders were injured. Police intervened and neutralized the raid after an hour.
On 10 December 2018, Elders from Pokot and Turkana communities met in Kainuk (Turkana South, Turkana), and resolved to end cattle theft and killings.

During the week beginning November 26th, herders assaulted a farmer at Banita (Nakuru). The farmer claimed the group wanted him to vacate the land. The event is part of a spate of similar incidents in the area.

On 29 November 2018, bandits attacked a group of herders at Lobua near Gambela (coordinates for Gambela, Wajir, used), killing one, and wounding two. The bandits then stole 16 cows. The source notes that bandits were suspected of belonging to the Turkana ethnic group, though this has not been confirmed.

On 15 November 2018, a youth Pokot militia (whose members are reported to be between the ages of 10 and 14) shot and killed a herder at an unspecified location in Baringo North sub-county (Baringo, coordinates for Bartabwa used). The attackers fled the scene after the attack, stealing 22 head of cattle.

On 6 November 2018, clash between suspected pastoralists from Lagdera and Uchana communities in the area of Janju (Isiolo, close to Mado Gashi) in retaliation for earlier violence in the area.Three people died in the clash, including one 'raider' and two children, and an unknown number of people were wounded.

On 4 November 2018, clash between suspected pastoralists from Lagdera and Uchana communities in Mado Gashi market (Isiolo) after an earlier 'botched raid' by the Lagdera in Mata Bofu. One person was injured.
On 4 November 2018, two people were wounded in a 'botched raid' at Mata Bofu, likey in Isiolo south. The attackers were believed to be pastoralists from Lagdera in Garissa county.

On or before October 24th, three herders (out of a group of seven) were killed and another injured when bandits fired upon them. The herders were making their way from Kapoa to Ameyan market (coordinates for Kapedo, Barringo, used).

On 21 September 2018, a herder militia (believed to be Somali in ethnicity) attacked Muthungwe village (coordinates for Mutitu, Kitui, used). The group killed a man and seriously injured his wife, using machetes to do so. The motive for the attack is not clear.

On 20 September 2018, a suspected bandit shot dead two herders and a child in Kerio Valley or nearby area as a revenge for the family failing to share cows stolen by one of the victims and the perpetrator during a raid in Tiaty, Baringo county. The attacker later surrendered to the police.

On 5 September 2018, two people were killed following armed clashes between Gabra and Borana pastoralist militia over pasture in Horonder, between Moyale and Marsabit. The first person died during clashes on 5 Sept, while the second passed away the following morning. Three other people were wounded.

On 4 September 2018, a herder (of an unspecified ethnicity) was killed in the Nkoben area of the Maasai Mau forest (coordinates for Mau Narok used). This killing sparked two days of violence in Narok (see separate entries).

On or before September 3rd, herders grazing their cattle in Boni Forest (Garissa county) were reportedly detained and beaten by the Kenyan military. At least eight herders were beaten, some seriously, and they have been separated from their cattle. The KDF denied that it was conducted any operations in the area.

On 30 August 2018, local clan members torched 14 houses in Kapyego, Marakwet East as an act of revenge towards the relatives of the man suspected to have shot dead an area acting chief. The chief had been shot dead by herders on suspicion he was a cattle thief.

7 August 2018: Three Somali herders who were grazing their cows on a planted land in Ganze, Kilifi County reportedly attacked the land-owner with knives, seriously injuring him and his brother who came to his aid.
23 June. One dead and several injured after two groups of Wajir herders clashed over pasture land.
On 4 June 2018, suspected Pokot militia shot and killed three people in Lokori (Turkana East, Turkana).
On 3 May 2018, a suspected Pokot militia ambushed a vehicle in Kapedo (Tirioko, Tiaty, Baringo). Four passengers were shot dead: three students and the driver.
21 April. Cattle thieves engage Tugen militia in a gun battle. One Tugen herder killed, 50 cows stolen.
24 March. Cattle herders killed 10 in Lopurio area in Samburu North in communal violence.
On 14 January 2018, suspected Pokot militia clashed with a group of four Samburu herders at Lomirok area of Baragoi (Samburu North, Samburu). One herder was injured during the incident.
Around 7 January 2018 (as reported), an unidentified armed group attacked Cheptulel (Lomut, Pokot Central, West Pokot). They killed four people and drove away with around 400 cattle.

Around 7 January 2018 (as reported), suspected Pokot ethnic militia attacked a village in Marakwet (coded as Elegeyo-Marakwet, Kapsowar, Marakwet West, Elgeyo Marakwet) in retaliation of the attack of Cheptulel (coded separately). Two people were killed and several were injured.
On 6 January 2018, suspected Pokot and Marakwet militias clashed at Tot (Marakwet East, Elgeyo Marakwet). Two people were killed, and several others sustained gunshot wounds.

On 5 January 2018, cattle rustlers attacked herders in Chesegon village near Tot (Endo, Marakwet East, Elgeyo Marakwet). They shot dead five people and made away stealing 300 cattle. Four people were seriously injured during the fight with police reservists.

Police were patrolling the private ranches in Ol Moran and Ratia and were attacked by the pastoralists when they tried to evict them. There was an exchange of fire between the officers and the pastoralists who were all armed. The latter destroyed a vehicle, after which the police countered with fire in a 2-hour long battle.
Pokot bandits suspected to be from Tiaty, Baringo East raided Murkutwo in Marakwet East on Saturday, injuring two herders.
Pokot bandits suspected to be from Tiaty, Baringo East raided Murkutwo in Marakwet East on Saturday, injuring two herders. A similar attack took place at Kaben area, which killed one man.

Pokot and Tugen herders clash for several hours in Kapkechir after an attack by the Pokot. The Pokot attackers killed four Tugen herder and stole their cattle. The attack led to a protest in nearby Mochongoi.

Pokot and Tugen herders clash for several hours in Kapkechir after an attack by the Pokot. The Pokot attackers killed four Tugen herder and stole their cattle. The attack led to a protest in nearby Mochongoi.
Pokot raiders attacked herdsmen who were repairing an electric fence at Laikipia Natre Conservancy
Two herdsmen and a suspected bandit were killed in a shootout that lasted for more than an hour in Kapkechir village in Baringo.
In retaliation for the killing of a herder the previous day, a group of herders killed 2 men.
In Tigania East a herdsman was attacked and killed by cattle rustlers.

Herders in Bambo, Mandera, have discovered five bodies buried in a shallow grave.The five, four men and a woman, were reported missing by their relatives last week.The locals exhumed the bodies on Monday [3 July] morning and took them to Lafey Hospital.Medical personnel at the hospital told Nation.co.ke that a male body had bullet wounds in the forehead and the other bodies appeared to have been strangled.The five were from Fino Ward but their bodies were found in Warankara Ward about 65 kilometres away.

A police officer is admitted Nyahururu hospital after he was shot by herders during a security operation to remove illegal herders from the Laikipia Nature Conservancy. The herders and police engaged in a gun battle.

Herders from Isiolo and Marsabit are feared dead as they engaged each other in a deadly gun battle throughout Friday. Residents from the two sides said the herders exchanged fire that led to deaths estimated to be over 10 people. Both sides had casualties, but the Isiolo side reportedly lost more men.

Mukutan Lodge was attacked by herders seeking pasture. They exchanged gunfire with the security forces and burned down the lodge.

Herders, illegally trespassing on land, injure a police officer and burn homes in Miteta, Ng'arua Division in Laikipia when they were confronted by a police. The violence comes 24 hours after a similar confrontation near Rumuruti.
Armed herders trespassing on illegal land shoot and injure a police officer after they were confronted near Rumuruti.

Non-violent activity: Heavily armed Somali militia/herders are reported to have encorached onto farms in Kitui, armed with AK-47s and displaced unprotected farmer settlements.

On 24 December 2016, one person was shot and injured when suspected Pokot militia raided Chemwoyo and Murkutwo. Marakwet herders retaliated leading to an hour of heavy gunfire.

On 27 November 2016, a woman was killed and a 12-year old girl injured in a shootout near Lomelo between armed pastoralists. The Rift Valley coordinator dismissed reports that 14 people were shot dead.

At least four more people have been killed in raging armed conflict between Borana and Somali herders (Auliyan) along the Isiolo-Garissa border [northeastern Kenya]. The fighting took place in Tana village about 11km north of Garba-Tula town on Saturday [10 September].
A Borana man is attacked and killed by Somali herders in Garfasa, Isiolo County. The attack is believed to be retaliatory.

Nine are dead and six are injured in a fight between pastoralists and farmers in Tana River. Additionally, several houses were destroyed. The clashes between Wardei pastoralists and Mijikenda farmers occurred in Wachu Oda in Garsen. A reported 1,500 people displaced as a result of the clashes.

Five pastoralists are killed by unidentified gunmen at Wari walo village some 10 kilometres from Kenya border. Those killed were three children (two boys and a girl), their father and a close relative. The five had recently left Elmole in pursuit of pasture and water for their animals.

At least 10 pastoralists from Isiolo have been killed in clashes with Laikipia residents after the herders invade the area with hundreds of animals. The herders also shot two security personnel after they were ordered to vacate the land during the clashes.
Pokot militia kill a goat herder in Chemoe.

A group of cattle herdsmen blocked the Mai Mahiu-Narok road (B3) for several hours after several of the herd were killed when they were hit with a lorry. The herdsmen demanded compensation for their loss by the colliding driver. They barred police officers from removing the truck or the carcasses until the matter was resolved.
Two people were injured as herders from the Tugen community battled suspected Pokot bandits. The battle broke out at Chemoe, near the Baringo North and Tiaty subcounty border.
Samburu and Borana herders clash over a water source. Four killed, two each side.

Six Turkana herders have been killed during the afternoon hours following an attack by Pokot raiders on a village in Kaakong area in Kainuk location, Turkana county. Three women are among seven other people injured in the ongoing attack by cattle rustlers from the neighbouring Pokot region. There has been repeated conflict along the Pokot - Turkana border as competition for resources and cattle rustling take centre stage.
Five herdsmen sustained gunshot wounds during a cattle raid at Nadome village in Tiaty sub county, Baringo. The suspects are believed to be Turkana.

A group of farmers clashed with pastoralists over grazing land around Lake Naivasha. The farmers who claim to be members of the Mau Mau group accused the herders of driving their animals into the farms. Causalities not known or reported.

Six people were injured during a confrontation between farmers and pastoralists at Mtondoni area in Hongwe ward, Lamu West district. The conflict ensued when pastoralists were accused of driving their animals into the farms and destroying crops. The identities of the two groups is not known.

The more than 200 cross-border Ugandan-Pokot raiders attacked Apuko village in Pokot North and drove away the animals after a fierce morning battle with Pokot herdsmen and security officers. Causalities not known.
Residents of Tangisir village in Meibeki/Karuna ward lynched a herdsman after he admitted to defiling and killing a seven-year-old nursery school girl.
